title: Apple Pie (Pita sa jabukama)
intro: This is the pie my grandmother made every autumn, as soon as the apples were picked. The secret is tart apples; it is never the same with sweet ones.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and brush a medium baking pan with oil.
Peel the apples, grate them coarsely and squeeze them lightly with your hands so they don't release too much juice.
Mix the grated apples with the sugar, cinnamon and ground walnuts.
Lay two sheets in the pan, sprinkle them with oil and spread over some of the filling. Repeat until the filling is used up, finishing with two sheets.
Brush the top sheet with oil and cut the pie into pieces before baking, so the layers won't break.
Bake for about 40 minutes, until the pastry turns golden. Let the pie cool a little before serving.

comments.name: Jelena
comments.text: I made it with Idared apples and it came out great. Next time I'll add a little more cinnamon.

comments.name: Miloš
comments.text: Cutting before baking is spot on, the pieces came out nice and even.

comments.name: Snežana
comments.text: My mom adds a little semolina to the filling to soak up the juice. Worth trying that way too.

title: Proja (cornbread with cheese)
intro: Proja was always our weekend breakfast, served warm with a glass of yogurt. It is ready in under an hour and it always disappears.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and line a baking pan of about 20 x 30 cm with baking paper.
In a large bowl whisk the eggs, then add the yogurt and oil and mix well.
Mix the cornmeal with the baking powder and salt, then gradually stir it into the wet mixture.
Crumble the cheese and stir most of it into the batter, saving the rest for the top.
Pour the batter into the pan, level it and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the proja is golden and a toothpick comes out dry.

comments.name: Dragana
comments.text: I used half yogurt and half sparkling water, and it was really fluffy.

comments.name: Nenad
comments.text: It's best while it's still warm. The kids ate half the pan for breakfast.

title: Prebranac (baked beans with onions)
intro: Prebranac is a fasting dish that we cooked on Fridays and on Christmas Eve. Soak the beans the night before; the rest is just patience.
steps: Pick over and rinse the beans, then soak them in cold water overnight.

Drain the beans, cover them with fresh water, bring to a boil and pour off the first water. Cover with water again, add the bay leaves and cook for about an hour and a half, until tender but not falling apart.
While the beans cook, slice the onions into thin half moons and sauté them in the oil over low heat for about 30 minutes, until soft and golden.
Take the onions off the heat, stir in the paprika, then season with salt and pepper.
Drain the beans, keeping one cup of the cooking water. In a clay or ovenproof dish, layer the beans and onions, finishing with onions on top.
Pour over a little of the cooking water and bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 40 minutes, until a crust forms on top.

comments.name: Ljiljana
comments.text: I sautéed the onions for almost an hour, there's no rushing it. It tastes just like my mother-in-law's.

comments.name: Zoran
comments.text: It's even better the next day. I make a double batch and freeze half.

title: Sarma (stuffed cabbage rolls)
intro: There is no winter in our house without sarma. I make it in a big pot, because someone always drops by just as it's cooking.
steps: Separate the sauerkraut leaves and thin out the thick ribs with a knife. If the cabbage is too salty, rinse the leaves in cold water.
Sauté the finely chopped onion in two tablespoons of the oil, add the meat and fry until it changes color. Stir in the rinsed rice, half a tablespoon of the paprika, pepper and a little salt.
Put a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up the sarma tightly.
Chop the rest of the cabbage and put it on the bottom of a large pot. Arrange the rolls side by side, and tuck the ribs and bay leaves in between them.
Add enough water to cover the rolls, weigh them down with a plate and simmer over low heat for two and a half to three hours.
At the end, make a roux in the remaining oil with the flour and the rest of the paprika, stir in a little of the liquid from the pot and pour it over the sarma. Cook for another ten minutes or so.

comments.name: Gordana
comments.text: After cooking I put mine in the oven for another half hour, it browns nicely on top.

comments.name: Stefan
comments.text: I made it on my own for the first time and it worked. The plate on top matters, otherwise they unroll.

comments.name: Vesna
comments.text: I also add a little smoked bacon to the filling, it smells so much better.

title: Pork Goulash (Svinjski gulaš)
intro: Goulash is a dish you can't ruin if you give it time. I always serve it with mashed potatoes or homemade bread for dipping.
steps: Cut the meat into cubes of about 3 cm and chop the onions finely.
Sauté the onions in the oil for about ten minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the meat and fry, stirring, until it changes color on all sides.
Add the chopped carrots, pepper and garlic, then take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika and tomato paste.
Return to the heat, pour in enough warm water to cover the meat, and add the bay leaves, salt and pepper.
Simmer covered over low heat for about an hour and a half, stirring now and then and adding water as needed, until the meat is tender and the sauce is thick.

comments.name: Marko
comments.text: I used pork neck instead of leg and the meat was really juicy.

comments.name: Tamara
comments.text: Always take the paprika off the heat. I scorched it once and the whole goulash turned bitter.

title: Stuffed Peppers (Punjene paprike)
intro: In summer, when the peppers are at their sweetest, I cook this at least once a week. They are best the next day, once the sauce has settled.
steps: Cut the tops off the peppers, stems attached, and remove the seeds.
Briefly sauté the finely chopped onion in a tablespoon of the oil. Once cooled, mix it with the meat, rinsed rice, egg, chopped parsley, half of the paprika, salt and pepper.
Fill the peppers, but not to the top, because the rice will swell. Close them with the cut-off tops.
Stand the peppers upright in a pot, pour in the tomato juice and enough water to almost cover them.
Simmer covered over low heat for about an hour and a half.
Make a roux in the remaining oil with the flour and the rest of the paprika, thin it with a little of the sauce and stir it into the pot. Cook for another ten minutes or so to thicken the sauce.

comments.name: Marija
comments.text: Afterwards I move them to the oven for half an hour, they get a lovely color.

comments.name: Dejan
comments.text: I serve them with sour cream, the way my grandmother did.

title: Potato Moussaka (Musaka od krompira)
intro: Moussaka is our Sunday lunch when everyone comes over. It isn't complicated, it just takes a bit of slicing and some patience while it bakes.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and grease a baking pan.
Sauté the finely chopped onion in a little oil, add the meat and fry until it changes color. Season with the paprika, salt and pepper.
Peel the potatoes and slice them into thin rounds, then salt them and drizzle with a little oil.
Layer potatoes in the pan, then meat, and repeat until everything is used, with potatoes on top.
Pour in half a cup of water, cover the pan with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt, remove the foil and pour it over the moussaka. Bake for another 25 to 30 minutes, until the topping is golden.

comments.name: Sanja
comments.text: I slice the potatoes on a mandoline, it's quick and they're all the same thickness.

comments.name: Petar
comments.text: You should let it rest for ten minutes before cutting, it slices more neatly.

title: Beans with Sausage (Pasulj sa kobasicom)
intro: Beans were a must on Thursdays at my parents' house, and that habit stuck. With a homemade sausage it's a proper winter dish.
steps: Soak the beans in cold water overnight.
Drain them, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil and pour off the first water.
Add about two liters of fresh water, then the peeled whole onion, carrot, garlic and bay leaves, and simmer over low heat for about two hours.
Slice the sausage into rounds and add it to the beans for the last half hour of cooking.
Make a roux in the oil with the flour, take it off the heat, stir in the paprika and thin it with a little of the bean broth.
Pour the roux into the beans, season with salt and pepper and cook for another ten minutes or so.

comments.name: Biljana
comments.text: I cook mine with smoked ribs instead of sausage, it's just as good.

comments.name: Aleksandar
comments.text: At the end I add a little chopped parsley, it freshens it up.

title: Homemade Ćevapi (Domaći ćevapi)
intro: Ćevapi from a grill house are one thing, but these made at home in a pan hold their own. What matters is letting the meat rest in the fridge for a few hours.
steps: Put both kinds of meat in a bowl with the crushed garlic, salt, pepper and paprika.
Dissolve the baking soda in the sparkling water and pour it into the meat.
Knead with your hands for at least ten minutes, until the mixture is smooth and sticky.
Cover the bowl and leave it in the fridge for at least two hours, ideally overnight.
With wet hands, shape small sausages about 7 cm long.
Cook them in a very hot grill pan or on a barbecue for about 8 minutes, turning them so they cook evenly. Serve with finely chopped onion.

comments.name: Nikola
comments.text: I left it overnight and the difference is huge, they are so much juicier.

comments.name: Jovana
comments.text: I made flatbread to go with them and it was just like Sarajevo.

comments.name: Dušan
comments.text: I add a little ground lamb too, but they're great like this as well.

title: Oven-Roasted Chicken with Potatoes (Piletina iz rerne sa krompirom)
intro: This is my weekday lifesaver: everything goes into one pan and the oven does the rest. The house smells of rosemary afterwards.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Mix the oil, crushed garlic, paprika, rosemary, the juice of half a lemon, salt and pepper.
Peel the potatoes, cut them into wedges and spread them over the pan.
Coat the chicken well with the marinade, arrange it over the potatoes and pour any leftover marinade over the potatoes.
Add half a cup of water, cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for another 30 to 35 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the potatoes are tender. Squeeze the remaining lemon over the chicken before serving.

comments.name: Ivana
comments.text: I added a few red onions cut into quarters, they caramelized beautifully.

comments.name: Vladimir
comments.text: Simple and tasty. The foil at the start is the real trick to keeping the meat from drying out.

title: Spaghetti Bolognese (Špageti bolonjeze)
intro: When nobody knows what to have for lunch, I make bolognese and everyone is happy. The sauce can also be made a day ahead.
steps: Sauté the finely chopped onion and grated carrot in the olive oil for about five minutes.
Add the garlic, then the meat, and fry, stirring, until it breaks up and changes color.
Pour in the passata, add the oregano, salt and pepper and simmer over low heat for about 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted water according to the package directions.
Drain the pasta, saving a little cooking water in case the sauce needs thinning.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce and serve sprinkled with Parmesan.

comments.name: Teodora
comments.text: I add a teaspoon of sugar to the sauce, it takes away the acidity of the tomatoes.

comments.name: Marko
comments.text: The sauce freezes really well, I always make a double batch.

title: Podvarak (baked sauerkraut with pork)
intro: Podvarak is a dish that bakes for a long time, which makes it perfect for cold weekends. Sauerkraut straight from the barrel gives it the right flavor.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Shred the cabbage into thin strands, and rinse it if it's too salty.
Cut the meat into larger pieces, salt it and brown it in the oil on all sides, then remove it.
In the same fat sauté the chopped onion and bacon, take it off the heat and stir in the paprika.
Add the cabbage, bay leaves and peppercorns, mix and transfer to a larger ovenproof dish.
Arrange the meat over the cabbage, pour in about 300 ml of water and cover with foil.
Bake for about two hours, removing the foil for the last half hour so the cabbage browns on top.

comments.name: Radmila
comments.text: I made it with turkey for Christmas and it came out beautifully.

comments.name: Zoran
comments.text: With proja and sour milk, there's nothing better.

title: Đuveč (baked vegetable and rice casserole)
intro: Đuveč is summer in a baking dish for us. When the vegetables are fresh from the market, it doesn't even need meat.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Sauté the onions cut into half moons in the oil, then add the peppers cut into strips and cook for another five minutes.
Add the diced eggplant and zucchini, salt, and cook for about ten minutes.
Stir in the rinsed rice and the paprika, then transfer everything to a baking dish.
Slice the tomatoes into rounds and arrange them over the vegetables. Pour in about 400 ml of warm water.
Bake for about an hour, until the rice is tender and the tomatoes have browned. Sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

comments.name: Mirjana
comments.text: I added a handful of green beans too, they go really well.

comments.name: Olivera
comments.text: I served it with roast chicken and everyone asked for more.

title: Chicken Paprikash (Pileći paprikaš)
intro: Chicken paprikash was the first dish I learned to cook from my mom. It is best with homemade noodles or mashed potatoes.
steps: Sauté the finely chopped onion in the oil for about ten minutes, until translucent.
Add the chicken and brown it for a few minutes on all sides.
Add the chopped pepper and the peeled, chopped tomato.
Take the pot off the heat, sprinkle in the paprika and flour and stir well.
Pour in about 500 ml of warm water, season with salt and pepper and simmer covered over low heat for about 45 minutes, until the meat is tender.
Toward the end, remove the lid so the sauce thickens.

comments.name: Katarina
comments.text: At the end I stirred in a spoonful of sour cream, the sauce was silky.

comments.name: Bojana
comments.text: A quick, reliable lunch, it always works.

title: Homemade Chicken Soup (Domaća pileća supa)
intro: We cooked this soup on Sundays and whenever someone fell ill. Cook it slowly, never at a hard boil, and it will be clear as a tear.
steps: Rinse the chicken, put it in a pot and cover with about two and a half liters of cold water.
Put it on the heat and, once it starts to boil, skim off the foam with a spoon.
Add the cleaned vegetables in whole pieces, the onion with its skin on for color, and the peppercorns.
Simmer over low heat, just barely bubbling, for about an hour and a half. Add salt near the end.
Strain the soup, then chop the meat and carrots and return them to it.
Add the noodles and cook them for a few minutes. Serve sprinkled with chopped parsley.

comments.name: Svetlana
comments.text: The onion skin gives such a lovely golden color, I didn't know that.

comments.name: Nataša
comments.text: I make a chicken salad from the leftover meat, nothing goes to waste.

title: Veal Soup (Teleća čorba)
intro: Veal soup finished with an egg yolk and sour cream liaison is our festive starter. It isn't heavy, you just have to add the liaison carefully at the end.
steps: Cut the veal into small cubes and the vegetables into small dice.
Sauté the onion in the oil, then add the meat and fry until it changes color.
Add the vegetables, cook for another five minutes, then sprinkle with the flour and stir.
Pour in about two liters of warm water, season with salt and pepper and simmer over low heat for about an hour.
In a cup whisk the egg yolk with the sour cream and lemon juice, then gradually add a few spoonfuls of the hot soup, stirring constantly.
Take the soup off the heat and stir in the liaison. Don't return it to the boil, or the yolk will curdle.

comments.name: Branka
comments.text: Adding the soup to the yolk gradually is the key, the first time mine curdled because I rushed.

comments.name: Dejan
comments.text: I also added a little chopped parsley at the end. Excellent.

title: Tomato Soup (Paradajz čorba)
intro: This is the soup I adored as a child, with a little rice and lots of parsley. In summer I make it with fresh tomatoes, in winter with jarred tomato juice.
steps: Pour boiling water over the tomatoes, peel and chop them.
Sauté the finely chopped onion in the oil, then sprinkle with the flour and stir briefly.
Add the tomatoes and cook for about ten minutes, until they break down. If you want a smooth soup, blend them.
Pour in about a liter of water, add the rinsed rice, the sugar and salt.
Cook for another 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Serve sprinkled with finely chopped parsley.

comments.name: Maja
comments.text: I made it with jarred juice and it was done in half an hour. The kids love it.

comments.name: Ksenija
comments.text: I used small noodles instead of rice, equally nice.

title: Vegetable Soup (Čorba od povrća)
intro: When the fridge holds a little of every vegetable, this soup happens. It is a bit different every time, and always good.
steps: Clean all the vegetables and cut them into small dice, and the green beans into small pieces.
Sauté the onion and carrots in the oil for about five minutes.
Add the remaining vegetables and cook for another five minutes, then sprinkle with the flour and paprika and stir.
Pour in about two liters of warm water, season with salt and pepper.
Simmer over low heat for about half an hour, until the vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.

comments.name: Danijela
comments.text: I added a little cauliflower too, it fit in nicely.

comments.name: Petar
comments.text: With a spoonful of sour cream in the bowl it's perfect.

title: Fish Soup (Riblja čorba)
intro: My dad cooked the real fish soup in a cauldron on the Danube, and this is the stovetop version. Lots of onion and hot pepper, that's the whole secret.
steps: Clean the fish, cut it into larger pieces, salt it and keep it in the fridge while you prepare the base.
Chop the onions finely, put them in a large pot, add about two and a half liters of water and cook for about an hour, until the onions have completely broken down.
Stir in the paprika, tomato paste, bay leaves and hot chili pepper.
Carefully add the fish, salt it and cook over medium heat for about 30 minutes.
Don't stir with a spoon so the fish doesn't fall apart, just shake the pot now and then.

comments.name: Željka
comments.text: I added the fish heads for flavor and took them out afterwards. Thick and fragrant.

comments.name: Vladimir
comments.text: Shaking instead of stirring, just like my grandfather did. Hats off to the recipe.

title: Creamy Pumpkin Soup (Krem supa od bundeve)
intro: When pumpkin season starts, this is the first thing I cook. It's thick, lightly sweet and warms you like a blanket.
steps: Peel the pumpkin, remove the seeds and cut it into cubes. Do the same with the carrots and potato.
Sauté the chopped onion in the butter, then add the vegetables and cook for a few minutes.
Pour in the stock or water, add salt and simmer for about 25 minutes, until everything is tender.
Blend with an immersion blender until you have a smooth soup.
Stir in the cream, nutmeg and pepper and heat briefly, but don't let it boil.

comments.name: Tijana
comments.text: I toasted the pumpkin seeds and sprinkled them on top, fantastic.

comments.name: Ana
comments.text: Without the cream it's vegan and just as good.

title: Lamb Soup (Jagnjeća čorba)
intro: Lamb soup is cooked for St. George's Day in our family, but we also make it whenever we get good lamb. It is pleasantly tangy and very refreshing.
steps: Cut the lamb into smaller pieces and the vegetables into small dice.
Sauté the onion in the oil, add the meat and fry until it changes color.
Add the vegetables, then sprinkle with the flour and paprika and stir.
Pour in about two liters of warm water, add salt and simmer over low heat for about an hour and a half, until the meat is tender.
Whisk the egg yolk with the sour cream and vinegar, then gradually add a few spoonfuls of the hot soup.
Take the soup off the heat, stir in the liaison and sprinkle with chopped parsley.

comments.name: Slađana
comments.text: I cooked it with lamb neck and the meat was very tender.

comments.name: Nikola
comments.text: The vinegar at the end gives it that authentic taste. Excellent.

title: Lentil Soup (Čorba od sočiva)
intro: Lentils don't need soaking, which makes this soup my quick fasting lunch. It is filling and cheap, and tastes as if it cooked all day.
steps: Pick over the lentils and rinse them well in cold water.
Sauté the chopped onion and carrot in the oil, then add the garlic.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika and tomato paste.
Add the lentils and bay leaves, pour in about 1.5 liters of water and simmer over low heat for about 40 minutes, until the lentils are tender.
Season with salt and pepper near the end. If it's too thick, add a little water.

comments.name: Mirjana
comments.text: I added a teaspoon of caraway, it goes really well with lentils.

comments.name: Stefan
comments.text: The next day it thickens up and I eat it like a stew. Great recipe.

title: Shopska Salad (Šopska salata)
intro: Shopska is the salad no summer lunch is complete without. What matters is ripe tomatoes and good, rich cheese.
steps: Wash the tomatoes, cucumbers and peppers and cut them into cubes.
Slice the onion into thin half moons or chop it finely.
Put the vegetables in a bowl, add salt, drizzle with the oil and vinegar and toss.
Grate or crumble the white cheese over the salad in a thick layer and serve right away.

comments.name: Gordana
comments.text: I put parsley over the cheese, it looks nice and smells great.

comments.name: Aleksandar
comments.text: With roasted peppers instead of fresh ones it's even better.

title: Serbian Salad (Srpska salata)
intro: The simplest salad in the world, but only if the vegetables are the real thing, straight from the market. The hot chili pepper is a must.
steps: Wash the vegetables and cut the tomato and cucumber into slices and the peppers into rings.
Slice the onion into thin rings and chop the chili pepper finely.
Put everything in a bowl and add salt.
Drizzle with the oil and vinegar, toss and leave for five minutes so the vegetables release their juices before serving.

comments.name: Zorica
comments.text: It's best with grilled meat, and you mop up the juice from the bowl with bread.

comments.name: Marko
comments.text: I used red onion, it's milder and looks nicer in the salad.

title: Sauerkraut Salad (Salata od kiselog kupusa)
intro: In winter this is the salad served with every lunch. If you have cabbage from a homemade barrel, it needs almost nothing.
steps: Cut the cabbage into thin strands. If it's too salty, rinse it briefly in cold water and drain well.
Slice the spring onions into rings.
Mix the cabbage and onions in a bowl, drizzle with the oil and toss.
Sprinkle with the paprika and pepper just before serving.

comments.name: Dragana
comments.text: With beans you can't do without this salad.

comments.name: Olivera
comments.text: I add a little grated carrot for color.

title: Potato Salad (Krompir salata)
intro: Potato salad is my favorite side with breaded fish and schnitzel. Dress it while the potatoes are still warm so they soak up all the flavor.
steps: Wash the potatoes and boil them in their skins in salted water for about 25 minutes, until tender.
Drain them, let them cool briefly, then peel and slice into rounds.
Slice the onion into thin half moons and chop the parsley finely.
While the potatoes are still warm, dress them with the oil and vinegar, add the onion, salt and pepper and toss gently.
Sprinkle with the parsley and let it sit for at least 15 minutes to blend before serving.

comments.name: Jovana
comments.text: Dressing it while warm makes a huge difference, thanks for the tip.

comments.name: Biljana
comments.text: I add a little mustard to the dressing, the kids really like it.

title: Roasted Pepper Salad (Salata od pečenih paprika)
intro: The smell of roasting peppers in the kitchen is the smell of September to me. This salad keeps in the fridge for several days and only gets better.
steps: Wash and dry the peppers and roast them in an oven preheated to 220 °C for about 30 minutes, turning them, until the skin blackens in spots.
Put the roasted peppers in a bowl, cover it and leave for 15 minutes to steam.
Peel the peppers and remove the seeds.
Arrange them in a dish, salt them and sprinkle with finely chopped garlic and parsley.
Drizzle with the oil and vinegar and let sit for at least half an hour before serving.

comments.name: Snežana
comments.text: Covering the bowl to let them steam is worth its weight in gold, the skin just slips off.

comments.name: Nenad
comments.text: With white cheese and proja, that's a whole meal.

title: Oven-Roasted New Potatoes (Mladi krompir iz rerne)
intro: As soon as new potatoes show up at the market, this is our side for everything. You don't even have to peel them, just scrub them well.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Scrub the potatoes well with a brush and cut larger ones in half.
Toss them with the oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, salt and pepper.
Spread the potatoes in a pan in a single layer and roast for about 40 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Sprinkle with chopped spring onions and serve warm.

comments.name: Teodora
comments.text: A single layer matters, when I crowd them they don't get crisp.

comments.name: Petar
comments.text: Before serving I added a little sour cream with garlic, excellent.

title: Greek Salad (Grčka salata)
intro: I fell in love with this salad on a seaside holiday and have made it ever since whenever it's hot. With a piece of bread it's enough for a light dinner too.
steps: Cut the tomatoes and cucumber into larger pieces and the pepper and onion into rings.
Put the vegetables in a bowl, add the olives and salt lightly.
Drizzle with the olive oil and toss.
Top with the feta, either as one whole slab or coarsely crumbled, and sprinkle with oregano.

comments.name: Ivana
comments.text: It's also great with our white cheese if you don't have feta.

comments.name: Katarina
comments.text: A squeeze of lemon juice and it's perfect.

title: Beet Salad (Salata od cvekle)
intro: Beet salad is my grandmother's winter salad, which she always made to go with roasts. Make it a day ahead and it will taste even better.
steps: Wash the beets and boil them in their skins for about 45 minutes, until a knife slides through easily.
Drain them, let them cool and peel them, preferably wearing gloves.
Cut them into thin rounds or strips.
Mix the vinegar, oil, sugar, salt and caraway with a little water and pour over the beets.
Leave in the fridge for at least a few hours before serving.

comments.name: Ljiljana
comments.text: I roast mine in foil instead of boiling, it's sweeter.

comments.name: Sanja
comments.text: A little grated horseradish on top and that's it.

title: Pogača (soft festive bread)
intro: A soft pogača was on our table for every slava and every birthday. The dough loves a warm kitchen and a little patience.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in a little of the lukewarm milk with the sugar and leave for about ten minutes until foamy.
Add the salt, the activated yeast, the rest of the milk and the oil to the flour, then knead for about ten minutes until the dough is smooth and soft.
Cover the dough and leave it in a warm place for about an hour, until doubled in size.
Knead the dough briefly, shape a round pogača and place it in a greased round baking pan. Leave for another 20 minutes to rise.
Brush it with the beaten egg.
Bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 35 minutes, until golden. Cover it with a clean cloth while it cools so the crust stays soft.

comments.name: Radmila
comments.text: A cloth over the hot pogača is an old trick, the crust comes out like cotton.

comments.name: Bojana
comments.text: I sprinkled it with sesame seeds before baking and it looked beautiful.

title: Cheese Crescent Rolls (Kiflice sa sirom)
intro: Kiflice were the first thing I learned to knead and they always vanish in one afternoon. I make a double batch and freeze half.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the lukewarm milk with the sugar and leave until foamy.
Add the flour, salt and oil and knead a soft dough, then leave it covered in a warm place for about 45 minutes.
Divide the dough into four parts and roll each into a circle, then cut it into eight triangles.
Put a little cheese on the wide end of each triangle and roll the crescent up toward the tip.
Arrange the crescents on a baking sheet lined with paper, brush them with the beaten egg and leave for another 15 minutes.
Bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 20 minutes, until golden.

comments.name: Milica
comments.text: I filled half with cheese and half with jam. They were gone in an hour.

comments.name: Danijela
comments.text: Frozen and then reheated, they're like fresh.

title: Homemade Bread (Domaći hleb)
intro: Since I started baking bread at home, I rarely buy it. This recipe is simple and forgiving, perfect for a start.
steps: In a bowl mix the flour, dry yeast, sugar and salt.
Add the lukewarm water and oil and knead for about ten minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover the bowl and leave the dough in a warm place for about an hour and a half, until doubled in size.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface, knead it briefly and shape a loaf. Put it in a baking pan or loaf tin and leave for another 40 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C and put a dish of water on the bottom for steam.
Score the top of the loaf with a knife and bake for about 35 minutes. The bread is done when it sounds hollow when you tap the bottom.

comments.name: Vesna
comments.text: The dish of water gave a beautiful crust. It's the first time my bread has worked.

comments.name: Dušan
comments.text: I used half whole wheat flour, I only added a bit more water.

title: Pogačice with Cracklings (Pogačice sa čvarcima)
intro: These little pogačice are my mother-in-law's specialty and there is no slava without them. It's a bit of work, but the flaky dough rewards the effort.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the milk with the sugar and leave until foamy.
Add the flour, salt, sour cream and the egg white, saving the yolk for brushing. Knead a soft dough and let it rest for half an hour.
Roll the dough out into a rectangle, spread a third of the cracklings over it, fold it like a letter and leave for 20 minutes.
Repeat the rolling, spreading and folding two more times, until the cracklings are used up.
Roll the dough out one last time to a thickness of 2 cm, score the surface in a crosshatch pattern and cut out the pogačice with a glass or cutter.
Arrange them on a baking sheet, brush with the egg yolk and leave for 20 minutes. Bake in an oven preheated to 200 °C for about 25 minutes.

comments.name: Mirjana
comments.text: The dough was really flaky, like from a bakery. It was worth the wait.

comments.name: Zoran
comments.text: They're best lukewarm, with a glass of yogurt.

comments.name: Branka
comments.text: I add a little pepper to the cracklings, it gives them something special.

title: Gibanica (cheese and phyllo pie)
intro: Gibanica is what we welcome guests with, for breakfast or alongside lunch. This one is juicy and light, with plenty of cheese.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and grease a large baking pan.
Whisk the eggs, add the yogurt, sparkling water, half of the oil and the salt, then stir in the crumbled cheese.
Lay two sheets on the bottom of the pan and sprinkle them with oil.
Dip each following sheet in the filling, crinkle it lightly and arrange it in the pan, until all the sheets are used.
Pour the remaining filling over the top and drizzle with a little oil.
Bake for about 40 minutes, until the gibanica is golden and risen.

comments.name: Svetlana
comments.text: The sparkling water is the secret, it came out soft and airy.

comments.name: Tamara
comments.text: I let it stand for half an hour before cutting and the pieces were perfect.

title: Zeljanica (spinach pie)
intro: In spring, as soon as the first spinach arrives, I make zeljanica. It is light, fragrant and just as good warm or cold.
steps: Wash the spinach, blanch it briefly in boiling water, drain and chop it. Squeeze it out well with your hands.
Chop the spring onions and mix them with the spinach, crumbled cheese, eggs and a little salt.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and grease a baking pan.
Lay two sheets in the pan, sprinkle them with oil and spread over some of the filling. Repeat until the filling is used up, finishing with two sheets.
Whisk the yogurt with the remaining oil and pour it over the pie.
Bake for about 40 minutes, until golden.

comments.name: Maja
comments.text: I made it with chard, also excellent.

comments.name: Slađana
comments.text: Squeezing out the spinach matters, otherwise the sheets turn soggy.

title: Meat Pie (Pita sa mesom)
intro: This is our home version of a meat pie, coiled into a snail. It isn't bakery burek, but the family likes it more.
ingredients: 500 g thicker phyllo sheets for pie
steps: Sauté the finely chopped onion in a little oil, add the meat and fry until it crumbles. Season with salt, pepper and paprika and let it cool.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C and grease a round baking pan.
Spread out one sheet, sprinkle it with oil, lay a second one on top and spread some of the filling along the longer edge.
Roll the sheets into a log and coil it into a snail in the center of the pan. Repeat, continuing the spiral, until the sheets and filling are used up.
Pour the sparkling water mixed with the remaining oil over the pie.
Bake for about 40 minutes, until golden and crisp.

comments.name: Nikola
comments.text: I served it with yogurt, like a proper breakfast.

comments.name: Željka
comments.text: The sparkling water over the top is a great idea, the sheets stayed soft inside.

title: Palačinke (thin crepe-style pancakes)
intro: Palačinke are the Sunday breakfast in our house, and the kids always fight over the last one. This batter makes thin, soft pancakes.
steps: Whisk the eggs with the sugar and salt, then add the milk.
Gradually stir in the flour, whisking so no lumps remain.
Add the sparkling water and oil and let the batter rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a pan and brush it with a few drops of oil.
Pour in a little batter, tilt the pan so it spreads evenly and cook the pancake for about a minute on each side.
Fill as you like: jam, chocolate hazelnut spread, walnuts with sugar, or cheese.

comments.name: Jelena
comments.text: The sparkling water makes them so much softer, I haven't made them without it since.

comments.name: Aleksandar
comments.text: I filled them with cheese and sour cream and baked them in the oven, for lunch.

title: Popara (warm bread and milk with cheese)
intro: Popara is the breakfast of my childhood, born from stale bread nobody wanted to throw away. I still make it today when I need something warm and simple.
steps: Cut the bread into cubes.
Heat the milk with a little salt until it begins to boil.
Add the bread to the milk, take it off the heat and leave for a few minutes to swell.
Stir in the butter and crumbled cheese.
Serve right away, while it's warm.

comments.name: Zorica
comments.text: My grandmother made it with water and lard, but this one with milk is much better.

comments.name: Dejan
comments.text: The kids like the sweet version, without cheese and with a little sugar.

title: Kačamak (cornmeal porridge with kajmak)
intro: Kačamak with kajmak and sour milk is a breakfast that holds you until lunch. Stir it vigorously, that is half the success.
steps: Heat the salted water in a pot and, once it begins to boil, pour the cornmeal in a mound into the center. Do not stir.
Make a hole in the middle of the mound with a wooden spoon and cook over low heat for 20 minutes.
Pour some of the water off into a cup, then stir the kačamak vigorously and mash it with the spoon.
If needed, add back a little of the poured-off water and stir until you have a smooth, thick mass.
With a spoon dipped in butter, scoop the kačamak onto plates and top with kajmak. Serve with sour milk.

comments.name: Radmila
comments.text: This is exactly how my mom cooked it in Šumadija. Thank you for the memory.

comments.name: Petar
comments.text: I top mine with cracklings and a little lard, for cold days.

title: Uštipci (fried dough puffs)
intro: When uštipci are frying, the whole building knows it's Saturday morning at our place. They are soft inside and crisp outside.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in a little of the lukewarm water with the sugar and leave until foamy.
Add the salt, egg, yeast and the rest of the water to the flour and stir with a spoon into a thick, sticky batter.
Cover the bowl and leave it in a warm place for about an hour, until the batter has risen and is bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deeper pot over medium heat.
Scoop out the batter with a spoon dipped in oil and lower it into the hot oil. Fry the uštipci until golden on all sides.
Lift them out onto paper towels to drain. Serve with cheese and kajmak, or with jam.

comments.name: Katarina
comments.text: The spoon dipped in oil is the trick I was missing, the dough doesn't stick anymore.

comments.name: Marija
comments.text: The oil must not be too hot, or they stay raw in the middle. On medium heat they're perfect.

title: Prženice (French toast, Balkan style)
intro: Prženice are the quickest way to turn stale bread into a favorite breakfast. We serve them with cheese and yogurt, and the kids like them with jam.
steps: In a shallow dish whisk the eggs with the milk and salt.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Dip the bread slices in the egg on both sides so they soak up well.
Fry them for two minutes on each side, until golden.
Lift them out onto paper towels and serve warm, with the cheese.

comments.name: Nataša
comments.text: For the kids I add a little cinnamon and sugar to the eggs, they love it.

comments.name: Stefan
comments.text: Bread from two days ago is best, it doesn't fall apart.

title: Scrambled Eggs with Peppers and Cheese (Kajgana sa paprikom i sirom)
intro: Kajgana is my breakfast when I'm short on time but want something warm. The pepper and cheese turn it into a proper little meal.
steps: Cut the pepper into small dice and the spring onion into rings.
Sauté the pepper and onion in the butter for about five minutes, until soft.
Whisk the eggs with a little salt and pepper and pour them into the pan.
Stir gently over low heat until the eggs set but stay moist.
At the end stir in the crumbled cheese and serve right away.

comments.name: Ivana
comments.text: I added a deseeded tomato too, excellent.

comments.name: Vladimir
comments.text: Low heat is the key, never dry scrambled eggs again.

title: Mekike (fluffy fried dough)
intro: Mekike made with yogurt are as soft as a little pillow, hence the name. With kajmak and cheese, Sunday breakfast is sorted.
steps: Mix the flour, dry yeast, sugar and salt.
Add the yogurt and lukewarm water and knead a soft dough that sticks slightly to your hands.
Cover the dough and leave it in a warm place for about an hour to rise.
With oiled hands pull off walnut-sized pieces of dough and stretch them into thin flat rounds.
Fry them in hot oil until golden on both sides, then lift them out onto paper towels.

comments.name: Biljana
comments.text: Oiled hands are a lifesaver, that's how I shaped them nicely for the first time.

comments.name: Nenad
comments.text: They're best with kajmak, while still hot.

title: Oatmeal with Apple and Cinnamon (Ovsena kaša sa jabukom i cimetom)
intro: Oatmeal is my autumn weekday breakfast. It's ready in ten minutes and smells like apple pie.
steps: Peel the apple and grate it or cut it into small dice.
In a small pot mix the oats, milk, apple and cinnamon.
Cook over low heat for about five minutes, stirring, until the porridge is thick and creamy.
Transfer to a bowl, drizzle with the honey and sprinkle with coarsely chopped walnuts.

comments.name: Tijana
comments.text: I make it with a pear when I have no apple, equally great.

comments.name: Ana
comments.text: I toast the walnuts in a dry pan for a few minutes, it makes a big difference.

title: Vanilice (vanilla jam sandwich cookies)
intro: Vanilice were the first cake I made with my grandmother, when I was so little that all I could do was spread the jam. There is no slava or New Year without them.
steps: Cream the lard with the sugar and vanilla sugar, then add the egg and lemon zest.
Stir in the walnuts and gradually the flour, and knead a smooth dough. Leave it in the fridge for half an hour.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 5 mm and cut small cookies with a cutter.
Bake them for about 12 minutes, so they stay pale and don't brown.
When they've cooled, sandwich them in pairs with jam and roll them in powdered sugar. Leave them for a day to soften before serving.

comments.name: Gordana
comments.text: They really are softer and nicer the next day. Patience pays off.

comments.name: Milica
comments.text: I made them with butter instead of lard, they're a little more crumbly but excellent.

comments.name: Snežana
comments.text: Pale vanilice are the real vanilice, good that you pointed that out.

title: Krofne (Balkan doughnuts)
intro: Krofne were a holiday when I was a child, and my mom made them only for special occasions. Now I make them, and there are never enough.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in a little milk with a teaspoon of sugar and leave until foamy.
Add the rest of the sugar, the vanilla sugar, salt, egg yolks, butter, yeast and milk to the flour, then knead for about ten minutes until the dough is smooth.
Cover it and leave in a warm place for about an hour, until doubled in size.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 1.5 cm and cut circles with a glass. Leave them covered for another 20 minutes.
Fry the krofne in oil heated over medium heat, first with the lid on, top side up, then uncovered on the other side, until golden.
Drain them on paper towels, fill with jam using a piping bag and dust with powdered sugar if you like.

comments.name: Jovana
comments.text: Covering the first side gives that white ring around the doughnut, just like from a pastry shop.

comments.name: Marko
comments.text: I filled them with chocolate hazelnut cream and they were gone in half an hour.

title: Poppy Seed Strudel (Štrudla sa makom)
intro: Poppy seed strudel is a must at our table for Christmas and Easter. This is a yeast dough, soft and thin, with plenty of filling.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in a little lukewarm milk with a teaspoon of sugar and leave until foamy.
From the flour, sugar, salt, one egg yolk, butter, yeast and milk knead a soft dough and leave it in a warm place for an hour.
For the filling heat the milk with the sugar, take it off the heat, stir in the poppy seeds and lemon zest and let it cool.
Divide the dough in two and roll each piece into a rectangle about 5 mm thick.
Spread the filling, leaving the edges free, and roll up the strudels tightly. Place them seam side down in a baking pan and leave for another 30 minutes.
Brush them with the second beaten egg yolk and bake in an oven preheated to 180 °C for about 35 minutes. Slice only once they've cooled.

comments.name: Radmila
comments.text: I pricked the strudel with a fork in a few places and it didn't burst. It's beautiful.

comments.name: Ljiljana
comments.text: I also put a spoonful of plum jam in the filling, it adds juiciness.

title: Reform Cake (Reform torta)
intro: Reform cake is the queen of slava cakes in my family. It is a lot of work, but once you slice it you see that every minute was worth it.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170 °C. Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then gradually add the sugar and beat until glossy.
Mix the walnuts with the flour and gently fold them into the whites with a spatula.
Divide the mixture into four parts and bake each layer on baking paper, in a 26 cm pan, for about 15 minutes.

For the filling whisk the egg yolks with the sugar and cook over a bain-marie, stirring constantly, for about ten minutes until thickened. Add the chopped chocolate to melt and let it cool completely.
Beat the butter until fluffy and gradually add the cooled cream, beating all the while.
Spread the filling between the layers and over the cake. Leave the cake in the fridge for at least a few hours, ideally overnight.

comments.name: Olivera
comments.text: The butter and the cream must be the same temperature, otherwise the filling curdles. I learned that the hard way.

comments.name: Bojana
comments.text: I made it for my daughter's birthday and everyone asked for the recipe.

title: Tufahije (stuffed poached apples)
intro: Tufahije are an old, simple dessert of apples poached in syrup and stuffed with walnuts. They always remind me of my grandmother and her kitchen.
steps: Peel the apples and remove the cores with a knife or corer, so that they stay whole.
In a wide pot bring the water, sugar and lemon juice to a boil.
Lower the apples into the syrup and cook them for about ten minutes, turning them, until tender but not falling apart.
Carefully lift out the apples and cook the syrup for another ten minutes or so to thicken.
Mix the walnuts with the sugar and a few spoonfuls of the syrup and fill the apples.
Arrange them in a bowl, pour over the thick syrup, chill and serve with whipped cream.

comments.name: Sanja
comments.text: I used Budimka apples and they held their shape perfectly.

comments.name: Dušan
comments.text: My wife adds a cinnamon stick to the syrup, I recommend it.

title: Čupavci (chocolate coconut sponge squares)
intro: Čupavci are the cake the kids in my house loved helping with the most, because everyone ends up covered in chocolate. They are always the first to disappear.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and line a baking pan of about 25 x 35 cm with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar, then add the milk and oil. Stir in the flour mixed with the baking powder.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake for about 25 minutes. Let the sponge cool completely, then cut it into cubes.
For the glaze melt the chocolate, butter and milk over low heat, stirring.
Dip each cube in the warm glaze, then roll it in the coconut.
Arrange the čupavci on a tray and leave them to set.

comments.name: Danijela
comments.text: A sponge from the day before is much easier to dip, it doesn't crumble.

comments.name: Teodora
comments.text: I use two forks for dipping, it's faster and cleaner.

title: Urmašice (syrup-soaked walnut cookies)
intro: Urmašice are small cookies soaked in syrup, the kind that go to every celebration. My aunt makes them best, and this is her recipe.
steps: First make the syrup: boil the water, sugar and sliced lemon for about ten minutes, then let it cool completely.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Cream the softened butter with the sugar, add the eggs and sour cream, then stir in the walnuts and the flour mixed with the baking powder.
Shape the dough into finger-sized logs and press each one over a fine grater to give them a pattern.
Arrange them in a baking pan and bake for about 20 minutes, until lightly golden.
Pour the cold syrup over the hot urmašice and leave them for a few hours to soak up the syrup.

comments.name: Mirjana
comments.text: Cold syrup on a hot cake, that's the rule. They came out juicy, just like my aunt's.

comments.name: Nataša
comments.text: I also make them with a little coconut in the dough, just as nice.

title: Plazma Torte (no-bake biscuit cake)
intro: This is a cake that needs no baking and looks like you slaved all day. My daughter asks for it every birthday.
steps: Cook a thick pudding from the milk, pudding mix and sugar according to the package directions, then leave it to cool completely, stirring now and then.
Beat the butter until fluffy and gradually add the cooled pudding.
Mix the ground biscuits with the walnuts.
Layer in a pan: biscuit mixture, then cream, and repeat until everything is used, with cream on top.
Whip the heavy cream and spread it over the cake, then grate the chocolate over it.
Leave the cake in the fridge for at least three hours before slicing.

comments.name: Maja
comments.text: The easiest cake I've ever made, and everyone thinks it's from a pastry shop.

comments.name: Ksenija
comments.text: I moistened the biscuits a little with milk, it was even juicier.

title: Sour Cherry Cake (Kolač sa višnjama)
intro: This is my quick cake for guests who announce they're coming an hour ahead. Sour cherries from the freezer work just as well as fresh.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and line a baking pan of about 25 x 35 cm with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar and vanilla sugar until fluffy.
Add the yogurt and oil, then stir in the flour mixed with the baking powder.
Pour the batter into the pan and spread the cherries evenly over the top. If they are frozen, drain them first and toss them in a little flour.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until a toothpick comes out dry.
Dust the cooled cake with powdered sugar and cut it into squares.

comments.name: Tamara
comments.text: The cherries tossed in flour didn't sink to the bottom, it makes a lovely cross-section.

comments.name: Zorica
comments.text: I made it with apricots too, it's excellent.

title: Ajvar (roasted red pepper spread)
intro: Making ajvar is a family day for us, we all roast, peel and stir. It takes the whole day, but winter without it is out of the question.
steps: Wash the peppers and eggplants and roast them on the stove, on a grill or in an oven at 220 °C, until the skin blackens and comes loose.
Put the roasted vegetables in a pot, cover and leave them to steam, then peel them and remove the seeds. Leave them to drain in a colander.
Grind the vegetables in a meat grinder or chop them finely.
In a wide, heavy-bottomed pot heat half of the oil, add the ground vegetables and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Gradually add the rest of the oil and cook for two to three hours, until the ajvar is thick and the oil starts to separate.
Near the end add the salt, sugar, vinegar and crushed garlic and cook for another ten minutes or so.
Spoon the hot ajvar into hot, clean jars, top with a little hot oil and seal immediately. Wrap the jars in a blanket and let them cool slowly.

comments.name: Branka
comments.text: Draining the peppers overnight cut an hour off the cooking.

comments.name: Nenad
comments.text: We make it without garlic, but everything else is the same. A good recipe.

comments.name: Ana
comments.text: A long-handled spoon is a must, ajvar spatters like crazy.

title: Pinđur (roasted pepper and tomato relish)
intro: Pinđur is ajvar's faster cousin, made with tomatoes and more garlic. I like it even more, especially with proja and cheese.
steps: Roast the peppers and eggplants, leave them to steam, then peel and clean them.
Pour boiling water over the tomatoes, peel and chop them.
Chop the peppers and eggplants finely or blend them briefly, so a few small pieces remain.
Heat the oil in a pot, add the tomatoes and cook them for about ten minutes, then add the other vegetables.
Simmer over low heat for about an hour and a half, stirring often, until thick.
Add the salt, sugar, vinegar and crushed garlic and cook for another ten minutes. Spoon the hot pinđur into hot jars, seal and wrap in a blanket.

comments.name: Svetlana
comments.text: I added a hot chili pepper too, it's perfect.

comments.name: Milica
comments.text: It was my first time making preserves and it worked. Thanks for the clear instructions.

title: Mixed Pickles (Mešana turšija)
intro: A colorful row of pickles on the pantry shelf is the loveliest sight of autumn to me. It's indispensable with roasts and sarma.
steps: Wash the vegetables. Prick the peppers with a fork, cut the tomatoes into quarters, break the cauliflower into florets and slice the carrots into rounds.
Wash the jars and lids well and dry them in the oven at 100 °C.
Pack the vegetables into the jars in colorful layers, adding peppercorns and bay leaves between them.
For the brine boil the water with the vinegar, sugar and salt, then let it cool slightly.
Pour the brine over the vegetables so they are completely covered and seal the jars.
Pasteurize the jars in a pot of water for about 15 minutes from the moment the water boils. Let them cool in the water and store in a cool place.

comments.name: Gordana
comments.text: The cauliflower stayed crunchy until spring. Excellent brine proportions.

comments.name: Dejan
comments.text: I added slices of hot pepper to every jar.

title: Sauerkraut (Kiseli kupus)
intro: Fermenting cabbage is our autumn ritual, inherited from my grandfather. One barrel gives enough cabbage for sarma, podvarak and salad until spring.
steps: Remove the outer leaves from the heads, wash them and cut out the core with a knife, leaving a hole.
Fill the hole of each head with a spoonful of salt and pack the heads into the barrel hole side up, adding the bay leaves and peppercorns in between.
Dissolve the rest of the salt in the water and pour it over the cabbage so it is completely covered.
Put a clean board and a heavy stone on top of the heads, so the cabbage always stays under the brine.
During the first weeks, circulate the brine every few days: drain it through the tap at the bottom and pour it back over the top, so the cabbage ferments evenly.
The cabbage is ready in four to six weeks, depending on the temperature. Keep the barrel in a cool place.

comments.name: Zoran
comments.text: We also add a few quinces to the barrel, the cabbage gets a lovely aroma.

comments.name: Radmila
comments.text: Non-iodized salt is a must, with regular salt the cabbage goes soft.

title: Plum Jam (Džem od šljiva)
intro: When Požegača plum season comes, my house smells of cinnamon and plums for days. This jam is thick and not too sweet, just the way I like it.
steps: Wash the plums, remove the pits and cut them into quarters.
Sprinkle them with the sugar and leave for an hour to release their juices.
Cook over medium heat, stirring often, for about an hour, until the jam thickens.
Near the end add the lemon juice, cinnamon and cloves. Test the consistency by dropping a little jam onto a cold plate: if it doesn't run, it's done.
Remove the cloves, spoon the hot jam into hot jars, seal them and turn them upside down until they cool.

comments.name: Vesna
comments.text: The cold plate test never lies. Excellent jam.

comments.name: Olivera
comments.text: I used a little less sugar and it kept well until winter.

title: Strawberry Preserve (Slatko od jagoda)
intro: Strawberry preserve was served to guests with a glass of cold water, as custom requires. Choose small, firm strawberries so they stay whole.
steps: Wash the strawberries before removing the stems, then drain them.
Cook a syrup from the water and sugar until a drop of syrup starts to feel sticky between your fingers.
Lower the strawberries into the syrup and cook over medium heat without stirring, just shaking the pot now and then and skimming off the foam.
When the syrup thickens again, after about fifteen minutes, add the lemon juice and vanilla sugar.
Take the preserve off the heat, cover it with a damp cloth and leave it overnight.
The next day spoon it into clean, dry jars and seal.

comments.name: Ljiljana
comments.text: The cloth overnight is that old secret, the strawberries stayed whole and shiny.

comments.name: Katarina
comments.text: My grandmother made it like this with sour cherries too. Thanks for the recipe.
